Class Base64Codec

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.codec.transform.encoding.Base64Codec
All Implemented Interfaces:
Codec<byte[]>
public final class Base64Codec extends Object implements Codec<byte[]>
A byte-to-text-safe-byte transform: encodes any bytes as Base64 (RFC 4648) and decodes them back. The output is still a byte[], but one made only of ASCII characters, so it survives places that mangle raw bytes — text columns, JSON string fields, URLs, log lines. Turn it into a String with new String(bytes, StandardCharsets.US_ASCII).

Put this transform last in a chain: Base64 expands its input by a third, so compress and encrypt first, then make the result text-safe: 

Codec<Order> codec = factory.create(Order.class)
    .andThen(new GzipCodec())
    .andThen(Base64Codec.urlSafeWithoutPadding());

Decoding is strict: input containing characters outside the variant's alphabet is rejected with InvalidPayloadException rather than decoded to garbage.

Instances are immutable and thread-safe.
